bib.title: Prompt-to-Prompt Image Editing with Cross Attention Control

question: Can a text-conditioned diffusion model's generated image be edited by changing only the text prompt, preserving the original layout, with no user mask?
hypothesis: Cross-attention maps determine the spatial layout of the generated image, so injecting the source image's maps into a generation with an edited prompt preserves structure.
contributions: Analysis showing cross-attention layers bind prompt words to spatial layout
Prompt-to-Prompt editing: word swap, adding a phrase, attention re-weighting, needing no training, fine-tuning, extra data or optimization
Application to real images via DDIM inversion plus attention-derived masks

method.summary: Runs the diffusion process for the source prompt and edited prompt in parallel with the same random seed, and overrides the edited run's cross-attention maps with source maps (all or a prefix of steps, or only for shared tokens), or rescales one token's map. Built on Imagen's 64x64 text-to-image diffusion model; super-resolution used unchanged.
method.task: text-driven image editing with a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model

models.name: Imagen (64x64 text-to-image diffusion model, super-resolution stages used as is)
models.architecture: U-Net with cross-attention at resolutions [16, 8] and hybrid attention at [32, 16, 8]; text embedding fused via cross-attention

other.sr_models: 64->256 hybrid attention in bottleneck (32); 256->1024 cross-attention in bottleneck (64)

inference.decoding: deterministic DDIM sampling (sigma_t = 0) with a fixed random seed shared between source and edited generations
inference.samples: qualitative examples only; number of images, seeds or runs not stated
inference.prompting: source prompt P and edited prompt P*; edits are word swap, added phrase, or re-weighted token

parameters.tau: timestamp until which source attention is injected in word swap and added phrase; value not given
parameters.classifier_free_guidance: value not stated; lowering it improves inversion reconstruction but limits editing
parameters.attention_maps: kept separate per head; only text-token channels of hybrid attention modified

other.overhead: one diffusion step applied to both z_{t-1} and z*_t in the same batch, so one-step overhead vs original inference (as printed)
other.real_image: DDIM inversion x0->xT; or naive noise-then-denoise (DDPM) with attention-derived mask restoring unedited regions

baselines: same prompt with fixed seed but no attention injection (Fig 2, Fig 6)
eval.protocol: qualitative figures only; no quantitative metric, user study or benchmark

evidence.quote: we scale the attention map of the assigned token j∗with parameter c ∈[−2, 2]

results.claim: The method needs no training, fine-tuning, extra data or optimization.
results.quote: does not requires model training, ﬁne-tuning, extra data, or optimization

results.claim: Fixing only the random seed and changing the prompt gives a completely different image; injecting source cross-attention maps preserves layout.
results.setup: 'lemon cake' to other cakes, Imagen, DDIM, qualitative (Fig 2)
results.quote: naively feeding the synthesis model with the prompt “pumpkin cake” results in a completely different geometry (3rd row), even when using the same random seed in a deterministic setting

results.claim: Injecting attention through all diffusion steps can over-constrain geometry; limiting injection to early steps balances fidelity and prompt adherence.
results.setup: 'cat riding on a bicycle', bicycle swapped for car, airplane, motorcycle, train; injection 0 to 100% of steps (Fig 6)
results.quote: the optimal result is not necessarily achieved by applying the injection throughout all diffusion steps

results.claim: Image structure is already determined in the early diffusion steps.
results.setup: Attention maps of 'a furry bear watching a bird' at different steps (Fig 4)
results.quote: we can see that the structure of the image is already determined in the early steps of the diffusion process

results.claim: The overhead over normal inference is one diffusion step since source and edited runs batch in parallel.
results.quote: there is only one step overhead with respect to the original inference of the diffusion model

results.claim: DDIM inversion of real images is often adequate but fails on other images; lowering classifier-free guidance improves reconstruction but limits edits.
results.quote: reducing the classiﬁer-free guidance [18] parameter (i.e., reducing the prompt influence) improves reconstruction but constrains our ability to perform signiﬁcant manipulations

limits: All evidence is qualitative figures; no benchmark, metric, user study or comparison with baselines is reported.
Real-image inversion gives visible distortion on some images and requires the user to supply a suitable prompt.
Cross-attention maps are low resolution (network bottleneck), bounding precise local edits.
Tau, guidance scale, number of examples and seeds are not stated.

terms.definition: editing an image by changing only the text prompt while controlling cross-attention maps

lineage.note: mask-free but trains a network per input; textures only

lineage.work: Attention is all you need (Vaswani et al. 2017)
